product: IonQ sells trapped-ion quantum computers including IonQ Tempo, quantum networking, quantum sensing including InSAR and optical communications terminals, and quantum security such as ClavisXG, plus post-SkyWater US-based semiconductor foundry and advanced packaging services.
demand: Demand is rising sharply: Q2 2026 revenue of 80.1M USD up 287% YoY, a fifth straight record quarter, RPO up 297% YoY, and guidance lifted twice, to 450-460M USD for FY26 including SkyWater.
pricing_power: Pricing power appears limited and unproven. No price increases are cited; growth is deployment and volume driven, and estimated FY26 gross margin falls to roughly 33% from 42%, suggesting mix and acquisition dilution rather than pricing leverage.
competition: IBM, Rigetti, D-Wave and other quantum hardware makers, plus quantum-as-a-service providers and specialty foundries. IonQ claims merchant-supplier and vertical-integration leadership; analyst ratings are mostly Buy but include one Sell and several Holds.
team: Chairman and CEO Niccolo de Masi; Inder Singh as COO and CFO; Paul T. Dacier Chief Legal Officer. The board expanded Aug 24 2026 with Dr Eric Ball, ex-Oracle treasurer, and Timothy Baxter, ex-SkyWater chairman and ex-Samsung North America CEO. SkyWater CEO Thomas Sonderman leads the subsidiary.
market_strategy: Be the vertically integrated full-stack quantum merchant supplier for US and allied defense, government and commercial markets, using SkyWater domestic foundry capability for cost and supply-chain control across computing, networking, sensing and security.
bull: Q2 2026 revenue 80.1M USD up 287% YoY, fifth straight record quarter, RPO up 297%, FY26 guidance raised Sep 8 to 450-460M USD; SkyWater acquisition (Jul 31) internalizes US foundry capacity.
bear: Q2 net loss 1867.7M USD, EPS -5.08, adjusted EBITDA loss 120.3M USD; FY26 gross margin falls to ~33% from 42%; guidance raise is acquisition-driven; Mizuho cut target to 52 on Sep 9.
falsifier: Q3 2026 earnings (est. Nov 4 2026) showing FY26 revenue guidance below 450M USD or organic growth under 100%, or gross margin below 33%.
web_what_changed: Jul 31 2026 IonQ closed the SkyWater Technology acquisition paying 15.00 USD cash plus 0.4883 IONQ shares per SkyWater share, creating a vertically integrated full-stack quantum platform. Aug 5 Q2 revenue 80.1M USD up 287% YoY. Aug 25 two new directors added. Sep 8 FY26 revenue guidance raised to 450-460M USD including SkyWater. Public warrants expire Sep 30 2026.
web_not_known_yesterday: No new primary IR or SEC disclosure dated Sep 24-25 2026 was found; the latest primary item is the Sep 8 2026 guidance raise. Sep 23 2026 CNBC reported a claimed IonQ quantum breakthrough and an Nvidia deal, aggregator only. Effectively nothing material was newly known on Sep 25 versus Sep 24.
web_demand_price_volume_mix: Growth is demand and volume led. Q2 2026 revenue of 80.1M USD rose 287% YoY on record IonQ Tempo deployments and cloud utilization, with remaining performance obligations up 297% YoY. Mix broadened to about 50% international, 60% commercial and 25% multi-product. No price increases are cited; guidance assumes 100% organic FY26 growth.
web_suppliers: SkyWater, acquired Jul 31 2026, is now IonQ in-house foundry, the largest US-based one, with fabs in Minnesota, Florida and Texas and DMEA Category 1A Trusted Foundry status. IonQ also acquired Nexus Photonics for integrated photonics. Management says this removes dependence on external chip fabs; the prior constraint was outsourced fabrication and packaging.
web_customers: Concentration is not disclosed in the press releases read. Named customers and partners include Amazon Web Services, AstraZeneca and NVIDIA, plus memoranda with Anduril and Sandia National Laboratories, an unnamed US government initiative using 84 on-orbit optical terminals, and EPB. Government and large-cloud exposure looks meaningful; no single-customer percentage was given.
web_who_loses: Competitors that outsource fabrication lose a cost and supply-chain edge: Rigetti, D-Wave and IBM, and quantum-as-a-service pure plays. Standalone specialty foundries and non-integrated quantum key distribution security vendors also lose differentiation. SkyWater rival US foundries and suppliers displaced by IonQ internalized photonics and packaging are affected.
web_contradicting_evidence: Q2 2026 net loss was 1867.7M USD with GAAP EPS -5.08 and adjusted EBITDA loss 120.3M USD. Estimated FY26 gross margin falls to about 33% from 42%. The Sep 8 guidance raise is acquisition-driven and includes SkyWater, not purely organic. Weiss Ratings downgraded to Sell D- on Aug 21 2026 and Mizuho cut its target to 52 USD from 61 on Sep 9 2026.
web_if_management_right: FY26 revenue lands at 450-460M USD with 100% organic growth, RPO keeps converting, and vertical integration lowers future unit costs. IonQ demonstrates its 256-qubit system and error-correction results on its own hardware, keeps the merchant-supplier role for US and allied defense quantum, and White House quantum executive orders sustain government demand.
web_if_management_wrong: Cash burn and losses keep widening while SkyWater lower-margin legacy foundry business dilutes blended gross margin. Integration of SkyWater and Nexus slips, organic growth misses 100%, and the Sep 30 2026 warrant expiry removes a capital source. Continued equity issuance against a 2.0B USD pro-forma cash position pressures shareholders.
web_second_order_beneficiaries: Cryogenics, laser, photonics and control-electronics suppliers; advanced packaging and US semiconductor supply-chain firms; cloud providers hosting quantum such as AWS, Microsoft Azure and Google; defense primes and Anduril-type integrators; national labs such as Sandia; and test and measurement vendors serving quantum hardware.
